clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive MyD88 deficiency produces a clinical picture essentially indistinguishable from IRAK-4 deficiency, reflecting the adjacent roles of the two proteins in the same signalling pathway.
Susceptibility is narrow: recurrent invasive pyogenic bacterial infection, particularly Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
Inflammatory responses are blunted, so fever and acute-phase reactants may be low or absent despite serious infection.
Antiviral, antifungal and antiparasitic immunity is largely intact because TLR3 and several other pathways are MyD88-independent.
Infection risk peaks in early childhood and tends to diminish as the patient grows older.
Standard immunological screening is frequently normal, requiring a high index of suspicion.
Antibiotic prophylaxis, immunoglobulin replacement and vaccination against encapsulated organisms are central to management.
reference.pathophysiology: MYD88 encodes the cytosolic adaptor protein MyD88, which links Toll-like receptors (all except TLR3) and interleukin-1 receptor family members to their downstream kinases. On receptor engagement, MyD88 recruits IRAK-4 and IRAK-1 to assemble the myddosome, driving NF-kappaB and MAPK activation and proinflammatory cytokine production. Biallelic loss-of-function variants abolish this adaptor function and produce the same failure of early innate inflammatory responses seen in IRAK-4 deficiency, hence the shared susceptibility to invasive pyogenic bacteria and the characteristically muted febrile and acute-phase response. This germline loss-of-function state is mechanistically distinct from the somatic gain-of-function MYD88 variants that occur in certain lymphoid malignancies.
additionalInvestigations: Functional Toll-like and interleukin-1 receptor stimulation assays demonstrating impaired cytokine production
Baseline immunoglobulins, complement and blood counts to exclude alternatives
Blood film for splenic-function markers such as Howell-Jolly bodies
Aggressive microbiological sampling and cultures during infective episodes
Site-directed imaging guided by the focus of infection
redFlags: Invasive pyogenic infection with a disproportionately mild fever or acute-phase response
Recurrent invasive pneumococcal or staphylococcal disease in a young child
Clinical deterioration despite reassuring inflammatory markers
reference.prognosis: As with IRAK-4 deficiency, early childhood carries the highest mortality risk during invasive episodes, but prophylaxis, vaccination and prompt treatment substantially improve outcomes, with susceptibility decreasing over time.
pitfalls: Confusing germline loss-of-function MyD88 deficiency (an immunodeficiency) with the somatic activating MYD88 mutations found in lymphomas such as Waldenstrom macroglobulinaemia, which are entirely different clinical entities.
Using fever or acute-phase markers to judge severity, which can be dangerously misleading.
Assuming that normal routine immunology excludes the disorder.
Withholding early empirical antibiotics pending confirmatory signs of inflammation.
references: IUIS Expert Committee classification of inborn errors of immunity
ESID clinical guidance on innate immune defects
management: Give long-term antibacterial prophylaxis against invasive pyogenic organisms, typically penicillin or co-trimoxazole, targeting Streptococcus pneumoniae, Staphylococcus aureus, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Provide immunoglobulin replacement therapy to supplement humoral protection during the high-risk early childhood years
Vaccinate against encapsulated organisms, including pneumococcal, Haemophilus influenzae type b, and meningococcal vaccines
Treat suspected infection with prompt aggressive empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics at the earliest sign, since blunted fever and acute-phase responses mask severity
Educate the patient and family to seek urgent medical care with any infective symptoms, given the muted clinical picture
Undertake aggressive microbiological sampling, cultures, and site-directed imaging during infective episodes and monitor with a high index of suspicion
Offer genetic counselling and family screening given autosomal recessive inheritance, and manage under an immunology specialist
